Title: Levetiracetam versus Phenobarbitone in Neonatal Seizures – A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Gowda VK, Romana A, Shivanna NH, Benakappa N, Benakappa A
Comment: No statistical test, RR or CI reported for mortality. Phenobarbitone deaths are not stated explicitly as "0"; inferred as zero because 46 discharged + 4 left against medical advice = 50 randomised and no deaths are mentioned in the PB arm. Denominators are the numbers randomised (50 per arm); crossover non-responders counted in originally randomised group.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg IV first-line') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (open-label, parallel groups with crossover after failure)
Participant type: Neonates aged 0-28 days with clinical seizures (term and preterm), outborn, admitted to level III NICU
Recruitment source: Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health, Bangalore
Outcome measurement: Number of neonates who died during the hospital/NICU admission, out of the number randomised to each arm

Report_ID: All-cause mortality before hospital discharge (death during NICU stay)
Title: Neonatal seizures – Levetiracetam versus phenobarbital
Author: Prakash, Richa, Sahni
Comment: The paper reports only "p>0.05" (no exact p-value); the value 0.05 is recorded as a threshold, not an exact p. No effect measure (RR/OR) is reported by the authors. Denominators are the numbers randomised (42 LEV, 38 PB), consistent with the stated intention-to-treat analysis despite cross-over to the other drug when seizures persisted.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Phenobarbitone (PB, Group B) first-line') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: term neonates (≥37 weeks gestation) with clinically apparent seizures admitted to a tertiary NICU
Recruitment source: NICU, Department of Pediatrics, tertiary hospital in Bihar, India (April 2018 – September 2019)
Outcome measurement: Number of babies who expired during NICU stay out of the number randomised to each arm
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality before hospital discharge (death during NICU stay)

Title: Short-Term Neurodevelopmental Outcome in Term Neonates Treated with Phenobarbital versus Levetiracetam: A Single-Center Experience
Author: Falsaperla et al.
Comment: Outcome NOT REPORTED: this randomized trial (PB n=15 vs LEV n=15) reports no deaths, mortality, or survival data in any section, table, or figure caption. Only arm denominators (15 and 15, from Table 1 "Number of patients") are verbatim in the paper; event counts are deliberately left empty and must NOT be imputed as zero. Per the synthesis plan ("If a paper does not report deaths at all, leave the study out rather than assuming zero"), this study should be EXCLUDED from the mortality meta-analysis. Row recorded only to document the non-reporting of the planned effect [E1].; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Phenobarbital (PB) group — IV 20 mg/kg loading, oral 5 mg/kg maintenance') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: term neonates with acute symptomatic seizures within the first 28 days of life
Recruitment source: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, S. Bambino Hospital, University Hospital "Policlinico-Vittorio Emanuele", Catania, Italy (Feb 2016–Feb 2018)

Title: Comparative efficacy of phenobarbitone versus levetiracetam in the initial treatment of neonatal seizure
Author: Khan TH, Rahman MM, Banerjee M, Uddin ZM, Nahar N, Akther M
Comment: Arms assigned by drug name, not column order: the paper's 'Intervention Group' is levetiracetam and 'Control Group' is phenobarbitone; phenobarbitone recorded as group_1 (plan's treatment). Table-IV has typographical/alignment errors in other rows (e.g. 'Discharged 37 (34.0)'); the Expired counts 2/50 (4%) levetiracetam and 5/50 (10%) phenobarbitone are internally consistent. The p=0.473 applies to the whole Treatment Outcome block, not to mortality alone. Risk ratio not reported by the paper; left uncomputed.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ("Control group of paper — IV phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg loading dose (plan's treatment arm)") is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Neonates 0–28 days with clinical neonatal seizures, gestational age >34 to <42 weeks, birth weight >2000 g
Recruitment source: Special care baby unit (SCABU), Dhaka Medical College Hospital
Outcome measurement: Count of neonates who expired during hospital stay out of 50 randomised per arm

Title: A randomized controlled trial on comparison of phenobarbitone and levetiracetam for the treatment of neonatal seizures: pilot study
Author: Perveen, Singh, Upadhyay, Singh, Chauhan
Comment: Table lists levetiracetam in the first column and phenobarbitone in the second; arms were reassigned by drug name so that phenobarbitone is group_1 (treatment). Crossover design: non-responders switched drugs, but intention-to-treat analysis retains original randomised groups (n=30 each). Narrative corroborates total of 6 (10%) in-hospital deaths. No effect measure named by the paper for this outcome; p=0.67 reported (chi-square/Fisher exact per Methods).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Phenobarbitone group (IV phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg first line)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Term and late preterm neonates (>2 kg) admitted to NICU within 48 hours of birth with clinically apparent seizures due to perinatal asphyxia with HIE
Recruitment source: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, government hospital, North India (July 2014 - December 2015)
Outcome measurement: Number of infants who died from any cause before hospital discharge, out of the number randomised in each arm (Table 2)
